strategy.summary: Reproduce gh-26699 by building numpy at buggy commit b8853b27c188 and running the PR's new tests in numpy/_core/tests/test_function_base.py. On the buggy revision linspace(inf, inf, 2) emits a RuntimeWarning that the tests escalate to an error, so the test fails. On the fixed revision equal endpoints skip the inf-inf subtraction, no warning is raised, and the outputs match. Numpy is the defect site and must be compiled from source, so the test cannot run against a wheel. Python version and dependency pins are not stated by the evidence and are left unbounded.

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang)

strategy.test_command: python -m pytest numpy/_core/tests/test_function_base.py -k 'inf_equal_endpoints or inf_mixed_endpoints or nan_endpoints' -q -p no:cacheprovider
strategy.reproducing_test: numpy/_core/tests/test_function_base.py::TestLinspace::test_inf_equal_endpoints (primary); the companion tests test_inf_mixed_endpoints_warns and test_nan_endpoints are also selected by the command
strategy.success_criterion: Buggy b8853b27c188: test_inf_equal_endpoints ERRORS or FAILS because linspace(+inf,+inf,2) raises RuntimeWarning 'invalid value encountered in subtract' under warnings.simplefilter('error', RuntimeWarning). Fixed revision: test_inf_equal_endpoints PASSES, with no warning and exact equality to np.full(N, inf/-inf) for all listed N, endpoint=False, retstep, array-valued, and complex-infinity cases. test_inf_mixed_endpoints_warns and test_nan_endpoints should pass on both revisions, serving as guards that the fix is not a global warning suppression.
strategy.numerical_probe: python -W error::RuntimeWarning -c 'import numpy as np; np.linspace(np.inf, np.inf, 2)'

input_output_examples.buggy_output: array([nan, nan, nan, inf]) with RuntimeWarning: invalid value encountered in subtract

risks: The bug is in compiled-independent Python code in function_base, but the fix path depends on how the build was made. Verify the editable build actually picked up the buggy source at b8853b27c188 and not a stale build directory before reading any result.

The transition depends on FP invalid-flag reporting and the RuntimeWarning being raised. If the platform or build does not set the invalid flag for inf-inf (for example some wasm or non-IEEE-conforming environments), the buggy revision may not fail. test_inf_mixed_endpoints_warns is skipped on WASM for this reason.

The test_inf_equal_endpoints complex-infinity cases (for example complex(inf,inf)) depend on complex subtraction and may warn on platforms with different complex arithmetic, so a failure could come from that section rather than the real-valued path.
The PR date is missing and the reproducer was run on 2.0.0rc2, so the commit may differ from the era when the bug was observed. Dtype is not stated as a trigger, so float64 is assumed.

Only the default platform was evidenced. A defect that appears only under a sanitizer or a specific SIMD or BLAS backend would not transition on a standard build; none is named in the evidence, so none is planned for.
The environment's listed test_command (python -c numpy.test()) does not select a single test and was not used; the pytest -k selection is used instead.
Python and numpy versions are unbounded; no documented constraint or era ceiling was supplied for any dependency, so the build uses whatever the repository's build requirements specify.

oracle.reference_source: assert_array_equal against np.full(N, inf) and array literals in test_inf_equal_endpoints
oracle.why: Infinite equal endpoints have exact expected values with no rounding, so exact equality is the right check.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision linspace(inf, inf, 2) computes inf - inf = nan and emits RuntimeWarning. Under warnings.simplefilter('error', RuntimeWarning) that warning becomes an exception, so the test errors before reaching its assertions.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision equal endpoints bypass the subtraction, no RuntimeWarning is raised, and all assert_array_equal checks against exact infinite arrays succeed.
